question: Should OpenClaw treat the Codex app-server serverName, combined with the plugin app's registered mcpServerNames and the narrow codex_apps connector classifier, as sufficient provenance for silent destructive-action approval?
rationale: This is an authorization-boundary decision: the code can enforce the proposed invariant, but only maintainers can confirm that these upstream identifiers are stable and authoritative enough to permit automatic approval.

options.title: Confirm the proposed boundary
options.body: Approve serverName-to-app registration as the canonical provenance check, retain the codex_apps exception, and require live proof before merge.

options.title: Require stronger Codex provenance
options.body: Pause this patch until Codex exposes or OpenClaw carries an unforgeable plugin or connector identity rather than relying on the server-name mapping.

options.title: Disable silent app-ID approval
options.body: Remove automatic app-ID approval for non-connector requests and require an explicit user approval path instead.

recommendation.title: Confirm the proposed boundary
recommendation.body: Approve serverName-to-app registration as the canonical provenance check, retain the codex_apps exception, and require live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the stable connector identity and mismatch policy in this exact resolver through the merged foundation PR.
